sourceAnswer.duplicateProgressionIntent: Twenty-plus duplicates are intentionally a long-term endgame mastery chase, consistent with the user's intended Chinese-style idle-game reference set.

duplicateMasteryDecision.productRole: long-term endgame mastery for selected favorite characters and weapons, not a baseline completion requirement for every owned item

completionLines.functionalCompletion: The first copy contains the complete advertised role and is usable in normal progression.
completionLines.competitiveBreakpoints: Early duplicate milestones provide visible but bounded improvements; exact breakpoints are simulation-dependent.
completionLines.fullMastery: Twenty or more effective duplicate copies or equivalent deterministic resources complete the long-term skill track.

mandatoryGuardrails: No main-story floor, reset access, evolution access, required combat role, or advertised core skill requires full mastery.
The largest functional gains occur before the final mastery stages; later stages use diminishing marginal power.
Selectors, exchange currency, universal fragments, reruns, pity carryover, and overflow conversion provide deterministic progress.
Full mastery is not treated as the expected state of the full roster for free-to-play or monthly-pass players.
Simulation must report time and spend to first copy, useful breakpoint, and full mastery separately.
The UI must label full mastery as long-term mastery rather than unfinished basic ownership.
duplicateMasteryDecision.rejectionCondition: If a base copy feels incomplete or ordinary progression is balanced around twenty-plus duplicates, the system fails even though the long-term mastery chase itself remains required.

decisions.lockedDecision: Playable characters are cats and catfolk. Generic humans and unrelated fantasy species are excluded from the initial playable roster.
The active named party contains four characters. Temporary reinforcements remain a separate support layer and do not increase the persistent named-party size.
The full initial product target is 24 characters and 36 weapons. Floors 1-10 implement a deliberately smaller subset and may not pretend the full catalog is complete.
The first evolution is paid with free ruby granted by the first valid strong-new-game reset. It is not a zero-cost tutorial evolution and does not require purchase or advertisement.
Every 100-level evolution receives clear effects, UI change, and minor visual variation; bespoke full character art is reserved for larger milestones.
N/R/RR/SR/SSR/UR is a fixed base-rarity identity. Evolution and duplicate skill mastery are separate axes and do not relabel an N unit as UR.

The design target is a 100-draw hard rarity pity and a 200-draw featured pickup guarantee, with compatible banner-class carryover, visible counters, and deterministic exchange. Exact rates remain subject to probability simulation.
Each active character equips one weapon. Weapons have no randomized substat maze in the initial product.
A consistent free-to-play player who watches no advertisements can reach one featured-UR guarantee within a target window of 30 to 45 days.

Monthly-pass players target approximately 1.5x to 2x progression speed; high-spend stress personas are bounded to approximately 3x to 5x. Spending may not create unbounded power independent of tower and reset progression.
Initial live operations are lightweight: permanent content, pickup banners, and login events. Battle pass and dense overlapping limited events are deferred.
The reset receives an original Cat's Tower name. Dawn is merged, renamed, or removed so that only one reset system and one confirmation flow exist.

remainingNamingWork: Choose the final original name and narrative presentation for the reset.
Name ticket classes, mastery currency, and major evolution-art milestones.
simulationRequiredBeforePass: Base copy versus early breakpoint versus full-mastery power curves.
F2P no-ad, rewarded-ad, monthly-pass, controlled payer, and high-spend time-to-first-copy, time-to-breakpoint, and time-to-full-mastery distributions.
Twenty-plus duplicate mastery with selectors, exchange, universal fragments, reruns, pity carryover, and overflow.
First-reset ruby covering the first evolution without purchase or advertisement.
